newsitem.title: USA: U.S stocks end lower ahead of key economic reports.
newsitem.headline: U.S stocks end lower ahead of key economic reports.

text.p: U.S. stocks gyrated to a weaker finish as investors braced for the upcoming onslaught of economic reports, starting with Tuesday's third quarter Employment Cost Index and October consumer confidence.

"Some investors are locking in profits ahead of several important economic indicators due to be released later this week, specifically third quarter GDP (on Wednesday) and October jobs" on Friday, said Philip Orlando, Chief Investment Officer at Value Line Asset Management.
The Dow fell 34 to settle just off its session-low 5973.
It was the second time the blue chip index has closed below the key 6000 mark since first ending above the level on October 14.
The Nasdaq Composite lost seven to about 1216.
Losers beat gainers 15 to eight on moderate NYSE volume of about 384 million shares.

As in stocks, the long bond gave up morning gains to fall 7/32 to yield 6.83 percent. Private economists expect the Employment Cost Index to rise a moderate 0.8 percent, the same pace as in the previous two quarters and not showing a pickup in inflation that would spur a Fed tightening.
Consumer confidence is seen slipping to 110.6 from September's 111.8 reading.
Analysts attributed selling to ongoing Wall Street concerns that the Democrats will retake the House and to tax-loss related selling by mutual funds by month's end.

"There's nothing fundamentally wrong with the market. But there's the same worry that the Democrats will take Congress in addition to the presidency and that causes consternation among fund managers. That and year-end tax selling which has had an effect on technology shares," said Thom Brown, a managing director at Rutherford Brown and Catherwood.
Brown said individual investors would likely complete their tax-loss selling in November. "It's going to mitigate against seeing the market go a lot higher."

With the bulk of third quarter corporate earnings out, "it looks like a lot of good news is behind us. It was a good showing but there were warnings (from U.S. corporations) that things are not getting better short-term. They told of (negative) currency translations and margin pressures," said Michael Metz, Oppenheimer's chief investment strategist.
Investment Company Institute said new cash into stock funds was $17.42 billion in September versus August's $17.92 billion.

"AMG (which tracks weekly flows) indicated it has slowed down some more. It's more evidence fund inflows peaked earlier this year. And the higher the market, the more it takes to get it going," Metz said.

Among individual shares, Electronic Data Systems resumed last week's slide after warning of sharply slower growth in the fourth quarter. EDS was the most-active NYSE issue and lost five to 41-1/8 after a Morgan Stanley downgrade.
RJR Nabisco rose 7/8 to 28-7/8. Oppenheimer raised RJR to buy from hold, with a $35 price target if there is no spin-off of its food unit and $40-plus if there is a spin-off.
RJR reiterated that it sees no spin off of its food unit prior to 1997.
Stocks hurt after earnings news included Mercury Finance, off two to 10-1/8 and Physician Alliance, off 4-5/8 to 4-7/8. Transition Systems lost five to 8-3/4 after an earnings warning.

Loctite rallied 12-1/8 to 58-1/8 after Germany-based Henkel said it intends to buy for $56 per share the roughly 65 percent of Loctite it does not already own. Loctite, a maker of engineering adhesives, said it will review the proposal from its largest shareholder.
In other merger news, Mercantile Bancorp, off 2-3/8 to 49-3/4, and Mark Twain Bancshares, up 3-5/8 to 46, agreed to merge in an $855 million tax-free exchange.
Pall lost 1-1/4 to 25-1/8 and Gelman Sciences rose 1/4 to 30-1/8. Pall definitively agreed to buy Gelman, which ended a merger pact with Memtec, up 5-1/2 to 34-3/4 in U.S. trading.
Revco rose 3/8 to 29-3/4 after agreeing to buy Big B Inc for $17.25 a share. Big B rose 9/16 to 17-1/8.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 6.71 to 1215.89.
The S&P 500 index fell 3.66 to 697.26, its first close below 700 since October 10.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721
